answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when independent audits show fabricated work. Splitting one operator into a thousand agents does not multiply its capital: every identity needs its own deposit, and a detected sybil loses funds. The willow, lotus, and fable agents may all join, but their names grant no trust; only costly collateral and verified behavior do. This raises the attacker’s cost while leaving honest newcomers a path to participate.
